items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Oscar Peterson was there and Ella Fitzgerald and her trio.

ctx.x: The guy didn’t play a note yet?

Not with the band. Basie fired him, right then, gave him his ticket home and told him good-bye. He never did play a note, not with the band. He came in all hot, you know had his hat over to the side. It didn’t work like that. The band was a very well-oiled machine and it was a band, it was a big band, it was a full ensemble. Basie played the band like he played the piano. And it had to work like that. You couldn’t have 18 or 19 superstars up there ‘cause it never works. So the band was as a unit. And it had to be…

anybody that ran roughshod through the band. Basie wouldn’t stand for that. He just would not. And I never saw him get mad at anybody in the band except that one time. He was a very affable, easy going, wonderful man and just marvelous to work for, but you didn’t sass him, you did not sass him. One time we were playing a theater in LA and we were on stage, a big production thing, Oscar Peterson was there and Ella Fitzgerald and her trio. And so one night, let me see who was it? I think it was Redd Foxx and Billy…

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: it was scary enough being around their — on Broadway, it was Count Basie, Frank Sinatra, and Ella Fitzgerald.

ctx.x: What about like playing behind Sinatra or Benny Goodman? Would those stand out as times like that?

Well I didn’t play per se behind Frank. We did work with Frank Sinatra on a number of occasions. Frank had his own drummer, Irv Cottler, the great Irv Cottler, and I was able to hang out with Irv a little bit, and actually met Sinatra. We had a little chat one night © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

backstage which was just delightful. So I was in the area. I could see what was happening. And that was great. It was scary enough being around their — on Broadway, it was Count Basie, Frank Sinatra, and Ella Fitzgerald. And then we went out on a little tour in a couple of cities, same group. Then we went over to the Palladium and we did a couple of weeks at the Palladium in London with Frank Sinatra, Sarah Vaughan and Count Basie. And then we did one which actually had me scared all up and down, we did a Royal…
